🎙 Iran’s U23 wrestling triumph in US reflects national strength: Parliament speaker

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has described Iran’s dominant victory at the U23 World Wrestling Championships in the United States as a demonstration of the nation’s strength and determination.

In a message on Monday, Ghalibaf said the freestyle team’s triumph and the raising of Iran’s flag had once again brought the country’s name to the world’s attention, adding that its repeated successes stemmed from a deep-rooted tradition built on determination, faith, knowledge and hard work.
​
The Iranian athletes raised Iran’s proud flag on US soil while American officials had imagined, in their futile dreams, erasing Iranians’ homeland from the map, he said, praising the wrestlers for compelling their opponents to respect Iran’s name and flag.
​
Ghalibaf said the athletes had overcome their rivals through knowledge and action, winning a sporting contest that culminated in Iran’s national anthem being played on US soil.
​
This is not merely a sporting victory, but a manifestation of the strength of a nation whose children can command the world’s respect in every field, he said.
​
The speaker congratulated the wrestlers, their families and the Iranian people, and thanked the athletes, coaches, technical staff, wrestling federation management and everyone involved in preparing the team.
​
Iran secured the U23 freestyle world title with nine medals across 10 weight categories: four gold, one silver and four bronze. The team finished with 180 points to claim the championship convincingly.

🔻 ‘It’s too late Mr. President’: Araghchi mocks Macron for shifting blame on French unrest

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has harshly reacted to the recent remarks by French President Emmanuel Macron, pathetically blaming the US war on Iran for the out-of-control unrest in France.

“Too late to blame the war his ilk helped cause. The French people demand wholesale change, including freedom of assembly,” Araghchi wrote in a post on his X account on Monday, in reference to Macron’s concern about nationwide violent protesters, which he attributed to the US-led war on Iran.
​
“Mr Macron made his bed when he assured POTUS that he welcomes atrocities against Iranians,” the top diplomat rebuked him further, and said: “Listen to the future of France, Mr. President.”
​
Araghchi also shared a past video message, in which Macron was found expressing support for US President Donald Trump’s illegal and illegitimate war on Iran.
​
Saturday saw some of the worst violence in France in years, after protests which had begun about education and schooling conditions broadened to wider cost of living and other domestic issues.
​
Macron, while expressing anger at rioting and looting, described the violent protesters as those who attempt “to bring down the republic”, promising that they would “pay for their crimes.”

🔊 Iran wins U23 world wrestling title in US

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iran’s freestyle wrestling team has won the U23 World Championships in Las Vegas, the United States, with four gold, one silver, and four bronze medals, collecting 180 points.

The U23 World Championships took place in Las Vegas from October 16 to 19, with Iran finishing first with 180 points, followed by Russia with 171 points and the United States with 104 points.
​
For Iran, Ahoura Khateri (65kg), Mehdi Yousefi (79kg), Abolfazl Rahmani (92kg) and Abolfazl Mohammadnejad (125kg) won gold medals, while Ebrahim Elahi (70kg) took silver.
​
Ebrahim Khari (61kg), Ali Karampour (74kg), Reza Afshar (86kg), and Mohammad Mobin Azimi (97kg) won bronze medals.
​
Iran finished first in the team standings ahead of Russia, the United States, Türkiye, Japan, Georgia, India, Kazakhstan, Armenia, and Azerbaijan.
